title: The car crash that killed Warwick Dyer
summary: Returning from a ball at 3 a.m., Frank Johnson drove off the road, Dyer was killed and Polites broke his neck; he reflects on musicians' travel risks.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. Uh, did he die when he was with the Frank Johnson band?

Yes, um, we were coming back from a job, um, about a hundred miles, uh, north of Melbourne. And, uh, oh, well, it was, uh, we'd been playing at a ball. It was about three in the morning. Uh, rushing to get back, uh, rushing to get back in time to have about an hour's sleep before we went back to our jobs and, uh, going a bit too fast. Frank Johnson was driving. He ran out of the road. And, uh, uh, we, uh, went over the side, uh, all of us got injured in some way or another, but, uh, Bokka was unfortunate enough to be killed. He didn't know anything, he didn't know it to some day. Mm-hmm. Um, I got a broken neck out of him. It's still a bit gone. Um, seems to do the thing, though, musicians are always, uh, uh, a great risk because they're not going to be a bad guy. It's a great risk because they're always travelling, uh, late at night or early in the morning, and, uh, when they're all, uh, keyed up after playing music and having a few drinks and all that.
